title: Consist manifest v1
description: What is aboard a candidate, generated FROM the branch and never hand-written. This document's sha256 IS the candidate's identity: the human V-signs against it, the station's row 0 enumerates FROM it, and every downstream PRD, values_proven row and station-verdict cites that one hash. The failure it exists to refuse is a reader deriving a claim from an intermediate view instead of the artifact - on 2026-08-31 a founder V-signed against lane-framing prose believing join code was aboard while the station's row 0 read `compose ps`, which cannot see a spawn image, so a stale bot was exercised while the fills read cargo-green. One generated object, two readers, no gap.

train_id.description: The train this consist belongs to (e.g. `t26-01226`). Stable across re-cuts of the same train; a re-cut changes candidate_sha, not this.

base_sha.description: The commit on the base ref (normally origin/main) the candidate was cut from. Every diff in this document is against exactly this commit, so a manifest generated from a stale base is detectable rather than plausible.

candidate_sha.description: Head of the assembled candidate. The tree this manifest describes and the tree the station must build.

cars.description: One row per unit of cargo. A car is a PR where the commits carry one, and an `unattributed` group where they do not - never omitted, because a commit that reached the candidate without a PR carries no narrative, no value sign-off and no non-author review, and that is precisely what a reviewer must be able to see.

pr.description: `<owner>/<repo>#<number>`, or the literal `unattributed` for commits carrying no PR reference. A bare number is refused: this workspace holds five repositories and an unqualified `#1011` makes the reader work out which.

author.description: The commit author whose work this car is. Authorship is load-bearing on the relationship ladder, not decoration - a contributor's car merges under their own name.

commits.description: Every commit in base_sha..candidate_sha attributed to this car, in topological order.

surfaces.description: Product surfaces this car lands in, as top-two-level path groups (e.g. `core/meetings`). This is what makes the blast radius readable without opening the diff, and it is what the PRD derives its per-cargo rows from.

not_aboard.description: The `you might believe X is in` list: every same-author or same-theme open PR, and every considered-then-excluded commit, that is NOT in this candidate, each with the reason. The section is mandatory and is the point of the document - an omission here is indistinguishable from an oversight, which is why the generator refuses to run without an explicit not-aboard input. An empty array is legal ONLY with the single sentinel row {pr: "none-considered-excluded", reason: ...}; see `not_aboard_sentinel` below.

pr.description: `<owner>/<repo>#<number>`, a commit sha, or the sentinel `none-considered-excluded`.

reason.description: Why it is not aboard, in the words of whoever decided. `held for #1075 by founder` and `superseded` are different facts and the reader needs which.

image_closure.description: Every buildable image the diff's code lands in. SPAWN IMAGES ARE MEMBERS - they never appear in `compose ps` and are the exact hole row 0 fell through. Each row carries its own row-0 obligation so the station enumerates from here rather than from what it can see running.

image.description: Image name as the station knows it (e.g. `vexa-bot`).

dockerfile.description: Repo-relative path to the Dockerfile, so the claim is checkable against the tree.

built_by.description: What builds it in this train (`station-build`, `compose`, `lite`, a CI workflow). Names who owes the build.

row0_required.description: Whether row 0 (running bytes == built bytes) must be proven for this image before departure. `false` needs a stated reason in `row0_waiver`; silence is not a waiver.

row0_waiver.description: Why row 0 is not required for this image. Meaningless when row0_required is true.

reason.description: Which changed paths put this image in the closure - the derivation, so a reader can refute it.

generator.description: The tool and version that produced this file. A hand-written manifest has no generator string it can honestly carry, which is the intended friction.

notes.description: Generator findings that are not refusals: heuristics it applied, closures it could not resolve, paths it could not attribute. A best-effort derivation that says where it was guessing is usable; a silent one is not.

allOf.$comment: not_aboard_sentinel - an empty not-aboard section must SAY it is empty. A manifest may carry the sentinel row alone, or real rows, never both.
